newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bourse may trade in Dow Jones products.
newsitem.headline: German bourse may trade in Dow Jones products.

text.p: The German bourse Deutsche Boerse AG (DBAG) said it was considering trading contracts on the Dow Jones index over its systems, which would allow a pre-bourse trade on the index before U.S. markets open.

Werner Seifert, chief executive of the bourse, told journalists on Tuesday evening that the bourse intended to assess the interest in Germany and approach Dow Jones & Co, which holds the licence for the U.S. index.

He said trade in such a product could start an hour or two before Wall Street opens at 1330 GMT. Such plans were part of a broader strategy to improve Frankfurt's standing as a financial centre, he said. More details would be revealed in coming months.
The bourse announced on Tuesday that it planned to extend the trading times for all interest rate futures and options on German bonds or Bunds and shorter-maturity bonds or BOBLs.
The longer opening hours -- to 1700 GMT compared with the current close of 1530 GMT -- will take effect from August 1.
